name: orb_wide_range_fade_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is wider than 2x the 20-day average ORB range, the initial move has over-extended — the opening auction was dominated by emotional retail order flow, and institutional mean-reversion will pull price back toward the ORB midpoint. Wide opening ranges are the OPPOSITE of compression — they represent exhaustion at the extremes. Instead of buying the breakout, fade the wide range by selling near ORB_high and buying near ORB_low. This is contrarian to standard ORB strategies and profits from the ~60% of wide-range days where price mean-reverts to the range midpoint. The inefficiency exists because standard ORB logic always buys breakouts, even when the opening range itself is a breakout (from overnight levels).
mechanism: The opening range concentrates pending orders and stop-losses on both sides. When price breaches the range boundary, stop-loss orders from wrong-side participants cascade, amplifying the move. Breakout-following algorithms detect the breach and add momentum, creating a self-reinforcing move that typically persists for 60-180 seconds before the order book absorbs the flow.

indicators.name: price_position
indicators.formula: (close - ORB_low_15) / ORB_range_15  # 0 at low, 1 at high

conditions: RSI_14 < 25 (oversold at bottom of wide range)
RSI_14 > 75 (overbought at top of wide range)

exit.signal_exit: if ORB_high/low is broken by > 0.3 * ORB_range (range extension, not fading), exit immediately

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX wide ranges may continue expanding
filters.volume_filter: opening 15-min volume > 1.5x average (confirming wide range was driven by real flow)

weaknesses: Fading wide ranges is contrarian; when the wide range IS the breakout (news-driven, institutional-driven), the fade loses big as price extends the range
Wide range days are infrequent (~10-15% of sessions), making this a low-frequency supplement strategy
The ORB midpoint target may not be reached on days where price consolidates near the extreme instead of reverting, resulting in time-stop exits with small losses
prior_art: Crabel (1990) wide range days (WR4/WR7); Connors (1999) on fading extended ranges. Adapted from daily chart concept to 15-min intraday opening range.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
